text: Accnomos is built for UK businesses and the self-employed who get paid, and pay suppliers, through PayPal. Here's how it keeps the books.
Small businesses paid through PayPal still match the fees and the VAT by hand.
PayPal's data comes in, the AI proposes, code calculates to the penny, and you approve.

Press Sync PayPal, and Accnomos fetches every payment from PayPal itself: the gross, PayPal's fee and the net. A sale with no invoice in your books waits for you to choose its VAT, and nothing posts until you approve.
Turn on the Power grid to tick several PayPal rows and approve them together. Or just type: PayPal fees over five pounds.
Or just ask, in your own words. Did that client pay the arrears? Accnomos checks your books and PayPal itself. A stationery order last month, around £100? Exactly £97.79.
say: Or just ask, in your own words. Did that client pay the arrears? Accnomos checks your books and PayPal itself. A stationery order last month, around a hundred pounds? Exactly ninety-seven pounds seventy-nine.

text: The tie-out checks your books against PayPal's own balance, as of PayPal's last refresh.
Paying a supplier works the other way. When a bill falls due, Accnomos offers a PayPal payout. You approve it, PayPal processes it, and it posts only when PayPal confirms. A retry never pays twice.
If a customer disputes a payment, Accnomos builds the evidence from your books, and nothing goes to PayPal until you send it.
Everywhere in Accnomos, the AI proposes, code checks the figures, and you approve.
Snap a receipt, and the AI reads it. Code checks the totals and the VAT, then you approve.
Bank statements, PayPal, and all your other income and expenses are reconciled against your books, in one place.
Ask for an invoice in plain words, and add a PayPal pay link.
The nine VAT boxes are worked out by code and filed to HMRC's sandbox, with HMRC's own receipt.
With HMRC-ready reports, from VAT to profit and loss.
Or talk to it, and approve what it proposes.
Jobs, with their costs and margins.
And the books stay in your own OneDrive or Google Drive.
Everything you saw runs on PayPal's sandbox. Try it yourself at accnomos.com, no sign-in needed.
